elements.element: Audit frequency is limited to no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 states: “No more than once in any twelve-month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires “at least thirty days' prior written notice.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted during business hours.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 limits audits to “normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 permits verification “through an independent auditor.”

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires the independent auditor to be “bound by written confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 5%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 assigns audit costs to Vendor unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent, after which Customer pays reasonable audit costs.

elements.element: Vendor and its auditor may not directly access Customer systems.
elements.evidence: Sections 22.1 and 22.2 expressly prohibit direct access to Customer systems; Section 22.1 additionally prohibits remote access.

elements.element: Audit frequency is limited to once per year.
elements.evidence: The stricter limit of no more than once in any twelve-month period satisfies an annual frequency limit.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 15 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least thirty days' prior written notice, which exceeds the 15-day fallback requirement.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 10%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs to Customer when underpayment exceeds 5%, including underpayments above 5% but not exceeding 10%; therefore, the 10% fallback threshold is not met.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred position, so failure of the separate fallback cost threshold does not prevent acceptance at the preferred level. The redline is not minimal because it also narrows the audit to verification of Services usage and adds a non-disruption requirement, neither of which is necessary to satisfy the preferred position. The audit right and existing payment remedy remain effective without contradiction, although the duplicated system-access prohibition is unnecessary.
